title: Optimistic concurrency for profile edits
problem: Two browser tabs (or two people) can edit the same profile. Implement get_profile() and update_bio() with a version column so that a save based on an outdated read fails with ConflictError instead of silently overwriting the other save.
requirements: get_profile returns (bio, version) and raises LookupError for a missing user
update_bio saves only if the stored version still equals expected_version, increments the version, commits and returns the new version
A stale expected_version raises ConflictError and changes nothing
A missing user raises LookupError, not ConflictError
On the success path, update_bio sends exactly one statement: an UPDATE whose WHERE clause checks the version
contract: get_profile(conn, user_id) -> tuple[str, int]; update_bio(conn, user_id, new_bio, expected_version) -> int; class ConflictError(Exception)
expectedBehavior: alice and bob both read version 1; alice's save returns 2; bob's save with version 1 raises ConflictError; bob re-reads version 2 and his retry returns 3
edgeCases: Saving identical text still bumps the version
Missing user vs stale version (both match 0 rows)
Retry with a fresh version after a conflict
hints: Conceptual: the version check and the write must be one atomic step. Put the check into the UPDATE's WHERE clause and let the database tell you whether it matched.

Specific: SET the new bio and version = version + 1, WHERE id = ? AND version = ?. cursor.rowcount is 1 if you won and 0 otherwise. Zero can also mean 'no such user'; distinguish only on that failure path.

Implementation: after conn.execute(UPDATE ...) and conn.commit(): if cur.rowcount == 1, return expected_version + 1; otherwise call get_profile (which raises LookupError for a missing user) and then raise ConflictError.
evaluation: No SELECT-then-UPDATE version check on the success path
ConflictError carries a message a caller could log or show
